Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

case noun

an instance, a situation

also instance, if that’s the case, in that case, in such a case, in the same case

classical

Cic. Fam. 7.7.2: id sī ita est
Cic. Att. 6.5.1: quō tē, sī ita est, salvum vēnisse gaudeō
Traupman 95: sī rēs sīc habet

sī ita est

phrase

if that is the case; in that case

Latin needs no noun for “case”: “if it is so”, and for the other case sīn aliter, if not (Cic. Fam. 11.14.3). Since that is the case, quae cum ita sint (Traupman 95). Traupman also gives eō cāsū, in that case (p. 95); Cicero’s letters say sī ita est.

Examples

  • in Britanniā nihil esse audiō neque aurī neque argentī. id sī ita est, essedum aliquod capiās suādeō et ad nōs quam prīmum recurrās

    I hear there is nothing in Britain, neither gold nor silver. If that’s the case, I suggest you grab a war chariot and race back to us as soon as you canCic. Fam. 7.7.2

  • id sī ita est, omnia faciliōra; sīn aliter, magnum negōtium

    if that is the case, everything is easier; if not, it’s a big jobCic. Fam. 11.14.3

Other words

  • causa, causae f. — a person’s case, the position someone is in

    noun, first declension · also used · classical · Cic. Off. 1.112: alius in eādem causā nōn dēbeat; Cic. Att. 11.2.3: quī videntur in eādem causā esse

    in eādem causā esse, to be in the same case (Lewis & Short: = condiciō). Also a case at law (see case, at law).

  • cāsus, cāsūs m. — an occurrence; an emergency

    noun, fourth declension · also used · classical · Caes. BG 5.33.4: in ejusmodī cāsū

    What happens unexpectedly: in such a case, of a crisis (Lewis & Short: “such an emergency”). In grammar, the case of a noun (Varro, Cicero).

See also situation, at least, case, test case.
